summary:
Who: the Pad-and-Liner Mom. She is 30-45 (core mid-30s), months to years past her last baby, and back to moving. She pees a little on the sneeze, the big laugh or the jump. She gets by with liners 'just in case', peeing before she leaves and crossing her legs. Period-underwear wearers are not a target, because the CJ product is that category.
Awareness: problem-aware. She knows she leaks, but she doesn't know there is underwear made for that moment. Every ad names the moment and the word pee, leak or sneeze in its first line. The ads speak in brand voice or third person, never 'you leak', and use 'I/we' only from a real, disclosed tester.
Videos (9, all cold, no price): V1, a pad-in-hand voiceover, carries A2 'Not a pad, not a diaper' (Everdries video#14 at 275d, UltraDries video#6 at 193d). V2, a side-by-side, carries A3 'It's just underwear': the A-vs-B mechanic is Tier A, and the pad-foil version rests on one unranked ad at 180d. V3, a silent on-body clip with one moment line, carries A1 'The moment'. It joins two proven parts (Everdries video#9 at 275d, Revival at 139d), but the combination is untested.
Statics (2 formats, 6 ads): S1, a plain pad photo with a long story caption, carries A2 (UltraDries image #1-#3 at 202-209d). S4, a text card, carries A1. Its listicle version has Tier A proof (Carol image#1, 249d); the one-line cards have Tier B proof only. The on-body photo (S2) was dropped because a plain underwear photo with no overlay isn't top of funnel. It moves to retargeting.
Round 1 uses only the moments the live hero continues: the laugh, the sneeze, and jumping jacks at home. Trampoline, kids, gym and run hooks wait for round 2, after hero Card 1 is live and the wear test covers repeated jumps and a run.
Before any spend: take the fake reviews off the page, add the pixel (with health data stripped from the URLs), publish the guarantee terms and the L1 source, log the wear test, measure the sample's sizes, and freeze the hero copy.

avatar.name: The Pad-and-Liner Mom (quiz persona 'The Comeback')
avatar.one_liner: A mom in her 30s, back to moving, who pees a little on the sneeze, the big laugh or the jump. She gets by with liners 'just in case', peeing before she leaves and crossing her legs, because everyone says it's just part of life after kids.
avatar.profile: Age 30-45, core mid-30s (ICP 'Mara, 36'; #14 'I'm 37 and have two kids'). Years out, she doesn't call herself 'postpartum', so ads never say 'postpartum' or 'after your baby'. She talks on Reddit (r/beyondthebump, r/Mom, r/xxfitness, r/running) and scrolls FB/IG feed and Reels. She uses disposables and workarounds, NOT period underwear: a period-underwear wearer already owns the category the CJ SKU is, and no CJ-legal TOF angle can move her (no attacking period underwear, no 'upgrade'). Her leak is small in her own words: 'pee a tiny bit' (#19), 'a little leak that might look like a crotch sweat' (#20). That a light-leak CJ panty can serve her is a HYPOTHESIS until the logged wear test covers a sneeze, a laugh and a jumping-jack set. Quiz Q4 ('It can be a lot' gets the redirect line) screens heavier leakers out. Mood: wry resignation. She keeps it private (#4 'except my husband and mom'). She isn't burned yet because she hasn't bought yet, not because she's less skeptical, so every ad keeps the guarantee line. Identity: strong, capable, not old. 'Diaper' and 'old' repel her. Size risk: this segment skews larger; see flags (measure the sample first). Base: about 16 core rows in the bank, the largest sub-avatar per Doc 2.
trigger_moments: ROUND 1: the sneeze: 'peeing a little every time i sneeze after giving birth' (#34), 'I'm sick and tired of peeing myself every time I sneeze' (#119). 'With a cold', 'toddler on the hip' and 'shopping bags' are our inference, not her words.
ROUND 1: laughing too hard (#19). Matches the landing H1 'Stop! I'll pee myself!' and H2 'not crossing your legs'.
ROUND 1: jumping, shown as jumping jacks at home: 'or jumped up and down' (#19), double-unders (#14). Matches the 'the jump' bullet. Gated on the wear test covering a jumping-jack set.
ROUND 2 (held): the trampoline with her kids (#123, #124). The landing's first screen doesn't continue it until hero Card 1 is live.

ROUND 2 (held): the run: 'I don't pee when I do anything but run' (#10), 'I always go pee right before I leave' (#30). No run line on the landing, and runs mean repeated leaks the wear test hasn't covered.
HELD: heavy lifting (#154, mom of 3). Can be more than a light panty holds.
failed_solutions: Pads or liners for runs and everyday, plus peeing right before she leaves (#30)
Pelvic-floor PT: slow and costly, and sometimes told to stop running (#33, #128)
Skipping the jump or leaving mid-play for the bathroom (#123). Skipping jump rope / the trampoline park (#125, not mom-tagged, reads like a testimonial)
Crossing her legs before a cough or laugh (inference; the wording comes from Ridgeview clinic copy #90, not her voice)
Spare undies in the bag (inference; the only bank row, #6, is a pregnant woman, a held-back segment)
objections: 'It's just normal after kids, I'll live with it.' The belief is widespread (#16 'We have all done it'; #31 'pretty common... especially post childbirth'; #122 argues against it, which shows how common it is). Answered by 'Common? Yes. Normal? No.' once the L1 source is live.
'Will it actually hold or leak through?' (#1 objection bank-wide). Answered only by the 30-Night Leak-Test, never by a claim.
'I'm not wearing a diaper / it'll feel like a wet diaper' (#152, #67). Answered by 'Not a pad, not a diaper', shown as plain black briefs.
'Will it ride up or show under leggings?' (#109 'ride up in the back'). Answered only by real, unedited footage of the actual sample under leggings, mid-movement.

'Will it fit my body / will the waistband roll?' (inference; #117 is a Knix 'if you have a tummy' review, not post-baby). Answered by quiz sizing + Fit Promise, and only with true facts about the cut once the sample is measured.
'It costs more than a pack of pads' (6 mentions). Answered after the quiz by per-pair pricing; never in TOF ads.
her_words: "After having a kid, I honestly used to pee a tiny bit pretty much every time I coughed (or sneezed or laughed too hard or jumped up and down)." #19
"It's not like we pee a puddle around us, it's just a little leak that might look like a crotch sweat." #20
"peeing a little every time i sneeze after giving birth" #34
"I'm sick and tired of peeing myself every time I sneeze." #119
"It's been 8 years since my last baby, why do I pee a little when jumping?" #123
"I was jumping on my kid's small trampoline... and a little pee leaked out as if I sneezed." #124
"I always go pee right before I leave, and wear an absorbent period pad when I run." #30
"Trying for a squat PR, pee your pants. Double unders? Pee your pants. We have all done it." #16 (CrossFit, not mom-tagged; shows how normalised it is)
"I'm not out here telling everyone about it except my husband and mom." #4
"How to not absolutely pee myself during double unders? I'm 37 and have two kids." #14
avatar.why_first: 1) The largest sub-avatar in Doc 2 (about 16 core rows) and the ICP. Athlete-tagged rows (31) outnumber mom-tagged rows (20), but 8 of the mom rows are training moms, and an athlete-only lead has no landing line yet. 2) She's the best funnel match: the hero's laugh/sneeze/jump, then Q2 'After having a baby' and the NORMAL card, then Q3 'Pads or liners' and the REACT card. 3) Her own words describe small leaks (#19, #20). That fits a light-leak panty, but it stays a hypothesis until the wear test. 4) Not yet burned (she hasn't bought), so the guarantee line in every ad does the trust work. 5) Mostly problem-aware: only 2 core rows are solution-aware (#33, #122). 6) She needs none of the CJ-banned angles (period undies failed, burned skeptic, mechanism). 7) Live mom/moment hooks exist to model, though only at Tier B (Origin postpartum 316d, Mireva 321d, Revival 139d).
hold_back: Period-underwear wearers (Knix/Thinx 'just in case', #25, #29): they already own the CJ category, and the angles that move them are Lynmiss-only. Not a CJ TOF target.
Trampoline-with-kids and run hooks inside the mom segment: round 2, after hero Card 1 is live and the wear test covers repeated jumps and a run.
Perimenopause 40s: 4 rows, no proven 30-45 lead ad, no landing line, highest Meta 'you'-rule risk. Later, on a /match-r page.

Standalone runner, CrossFit or lifter campaigns: no landing line, and repeated or heavier leaks may exceed a light panty. NUMBER_SHEET §13 names the smaller/athlete segment as the fallback if the size run is small.
Pregnant or immediate postpartum (#6, #113, #151): temporary, sensitive, and pulls toward diapers.
60+ and heavy leakers: Everdries' turf, and the CJ panty is too light for them.
Night-time leaks: skip until the CJ back coverage is confirmed (O20).

awareness.level: Problem-aware, led moment-first: the first line shows or names the sneeze, laugh or jump with the word pee, leak or sneeze. It is never a 'do you leak?' question.
awareness.why: She knows she leaks and can name the moment. She doesn't know there is underwear made for it, so she improvises with liners, peeing first and crossing her legs. Many have normalised it (#16 'We have all done it'), and Meta rejects second-person condition lines. So the ad names the moment in brand voice or third person, she recognises herself, and the quiz asks the condition questions. The moment line must still say pee, leak or sneeze, or a stranger reads a liner or black-briefs ad as period or panty-line content. Solution-aware angles (period undies failed, burned skeptic) are Lynmiss-only. Product-aware and offer ads skip the quiz and belong in retargeting.
awareness.split: Bank-wide, 71-72 tagged rows (sources differ by one): about 40% problem-aware, 27-28% solution-aware, 26-27% product-aware, 6% most-aware. Reddit, where the 30-45 ICP talks: 52 tagged, 46/29/25%. Core mom pool (about 16 rows): mostly problem-aware, with only 2 solution-aware (#33, #122). Of the 46 burned rows, 40 are on retail review sites (Trustpilot 22, Amazon 12, PissedConsumer 3, Walmart 3), and 42 are non-Reddit. Only 4 of 52 Reddit rows are burned.
awareness.sophistication: Stage 4-5. The loud players sell age identity (Everdries 'over 60') and bigger mechanism claims. On CJ we can't run a mechanism or out-claim anyone. So we enter on experience: the moment she knows, plain black briefs she recognises as underwear, and the CJ enemy line limited to comfort and waste. Proof comes from the 30-Night Leak-Test and the Fit Promise, not from claims.
beliefs_to_shift: B2 (CJ wording): 'My options are liners and pads' becomes 'Liners bunch, feel like a diaper and go in the trash every day, and there are plain black briefs for the sneeze, the laugh and the jump.' No holding or performance comparison.
B5: 'It'll feel like a diaper or show under leggings' becomes 'It looks like plain black briefs.' Claim only what real footage of the sample shows.
B4: 'That stuff is for old women' becomes 'This is for women who laugh and move.' Show her standing or moving, never hidden.
B1 (beat only, once the L1 source is live): 'It's just normal' becomes 'Common? Yes. Normal? No.'
B3 (closing line only): 'It probably won't hold' becomes '30 nights to see if they hold, money back if they don't.'
awareness.tof_job: Earn the click, not the sale. In the first line or first 3 seconds, name the moment with the word pee, leak or sneeze (the sneeze, the big laugh, jumping jacks), in brand voice or third person. Name the workaround she'll recognise (liner 'just in case', crossing her legs). Reveal the category, not a mechanism: plain black briefs, on a real body, under leggings, moving. De-risk in one line (30 nights to see if they hold). Hand off to 'Find my match' (the quiz). No price, gifts, 'new', reviews, stats or mechanism.

funnel.what_she_lands_on: One hero for everyone today (leapproof.myfunnelish.com/LP). H1: 'Stop! I'll pee myself! / Common? Yes. Normal? No. / Find your match.' Subhead: 'Black briefs for women who'd rather laugh than cross their legs. The quiz works out your size and how many pairs you need. Then 30 nights to see if they hold.' Bullets: 'Feels like underwear. Not a pad, not a diaper.' / 'Built for the sneeze, the laugh and the jump' / '30 nights to test. Money back if they don't hold.' Carousel: group of women in black briefs, back view, the brief under leggings (slide 3; AI-generated). Button 'Find my match' (below the fold on mobile). H2: 'Picture the next big laugh, and not crossing your legs for it.' Then 3 FAKE named reviews, which must be removed; they hold the only trampoline, kid and gym-bag lines on the page. The first screen has no mom, kid, trampoline, gym, run, leggings or 'no line' text.
funnel.promise_chain: Ad: the moment (laugh, sneeze, jump) + 'not a pad, not a diaper'. Landing: the same words in the H1, H2 and bullets, then 'Find my match'. Quiz: Q1 replays her moment, then the WHY card. Q2 'After having a baby' gives the NORMAL card. Q3 'Pads or liners' gives the REACT card ('Pads bunch and shift the second you move'). Result: 'free gifts unlocked', '30 nights to see if they hold'. Offer: 'Your N pairs are ready, size X', then the pads vs Leapproof table ('go in the trash every day'). Checkout. Words carried end to end: MOMENT, NOT A PAD, MATCH, 30 NIGHTS. Price, sets and gifts appear only after the quiz. Trampoline and kids show up only at Q8/Q13 and on the offer page, which is why they're held out of round 1.
funnel.angle_code_reality: ?a= changes nothing on the page today. /LP, /LP?a=p and /LP?a=m render the same hero, and no /match-[code] clones exist. 'a' only passes through quiz, offer and checkout as an attribution tag. So every round-1 angle was picked to match the one live hero: A1 matches H1 + H2, A2 and A3 match the 'Not a pad, not a diaper' bullet. Use a=m on all ads (the only launch code in LANDING §7) and split angles with utm_content=moment / pads / underwear. Don't invent new a= codes until they're in the FUNNEL_PLAN §6 table.
funnel.rule_for_every_ad: 1) The first line or first 3s names the moment AND the word pee, leak or sneeze (sneeze, big laugh, jumping jacks), in brand voice, third person or a bare moment line. Never 'you leak / your bladder / after your baby'. 'I / we / us' only from a real, disclosed tester it's true for. An actor re-enacting a moment gets 'Dramatization' on screen. On statics, the first ~125 caption characters do this. 2) The ad ends on a line the FROZEN hero repeats: 'Stop! I'll pee myself!', 'Common? Yes. Normal? No.' (only once the L1 source is live), 'Not a pad, not a diaper', or 'For the sneeze, the laugh and the jump' (never 'built / designed / made for', and only after the logged wear test). 3) CTA = the quiz ('Find my match'), never price, gifts or sale. 4) Show only the real CJ plain black brief, on a real woman 30-45: full figure, mid-movement, under leggings where possible, no butt- or crotch-centred crops, no children in any round-1 ad. 5) The only enemy line is the CJ one, in US wording: 'Pads and liners bunch, feel like a diaper, and go in the trash every day.' Contrasts use only those attributes (bunch, shift, diaper feel, shows, trash), never 'fails / doesn't hold / wrong tool'. 6) 'Hold' only inside the guarantee. No absolute or comparative leak claims, mechanism, reviews, doctors, stats, eco claims or urgency.

angles.name: The moment: 'Stop! I'll pee myself!' (the sneeze, the big laugh, the jump)
angles.core_message: The big laugh, the sneeze, the jump: the moment women cross their legs and hope. There are plain black briefs for that moment, so she can laugh instead.
angles.awareness: Problem-aware, moment-first (the moment named with the word pee, leak or sneeze, never as 'you leak').
angles.proof: Tier B only, on 30-45 women. Real moment overlays on creative: Revival 1688978975632845 (139d, gym meme), Your Postpartum PT 1530319598830519 (113d, sneeze re-enactment), Pine Peak 869271709162736 text card (97d, 'Hoping nobody tells a really funny joke?'). Also Advanced Health 1015538471405847 'Sneezing Shouldn't Require Crossing Your Legs' (112d) and FPW 2181639299326800 laugh/sneeze/trampoline (103d). Origin's 'Leak when you sneeze?' runs on 8 ads at 126-372d, but as caption copy inside a 3-symptom checklist, not as a creative hook (the 24707440378884436 overlay is 'Symptoms Your Pelvic Floor PT Can Treat'). Origin card 870082525676896 (312d) sits in a DCO with a video, so its run time can't be credited to the card alone. Tier A carries 'sneeze' (~100) and 'laugh' (~110) in live Everdries body copy only. Honest gap: no Tier A ad leads with the moment.
angles.landing_handoff: H1 line 1 'Stop! I'll pee myself!' + H2 'Picture the next big laugh, and not crossing your legs for it.' + bullet '...the sneeze, the laugh and the jump'. Then quiz Q1 'When does it happen most?' and the WHY card.
angles.a_code: m (attribution only; same hero for every code); utm_content=moment
angles.why_it_suits_brand_and_funnel: It's the brand's own hero line and first non-negotiable ('open on the moment'), and the strongest word-for-word scent match. Laugh is the best match (the H1 is a laugh), then sneeze, then jump through the bullet. Every moment used here is on the landing's first screen. Trampoline, run and gym moments are not, so they wait.

angles.name: Not a pad, not a diaper (CJ enemy line: liners bunch, feel like a diaper, go in the trash)
angles.core_message: Liners and pads bunch, shift, feel like a diaper and go in the trash every day. There are plain black briefs for the sneeze, the laugh and the jump. Comfort and routine only, never 'pads fail'.
angles.awareness: Problem-aware (she uses liners or pads 'just in case' for the moment).
angles.proof: The most proven problem/solution angle in the set: 'Pads are wrong' + 'Replace pads' = 44 Tier A ads, 15 in a page top-10 (of 137 classified Tier A ads, so lower bounds). That top-10 strength sits mostly in statics: 8 of the 15 are long-form story statics (Life Beyond Leaks image #1, #2, #3, #6, #9, #10; Carol #5, #6). Five are fake-expert videos, one is a skit, and one is a voiceover (Life Beyond Leaks video#6). Videos: Everdries 1206351388295667 (275d, video#14, 2-6 Meta duplicates) and UltraDries 896552676720439 (193d, video#6). Live counts: Everdries 'pads' ~190 videos; UltraDries 'pads' on ~100/100 Life Beyond Leaks ads.
angles.landing_handoff: Bullet 'Feels like underwear. Not a pad, not a diaper.' Then quiz Q3 'Pads or liners' gives the REACT card 'Pads bunch and shift the second you move', and the offer's pads vs Leapproof table ('go in the trash every day').
angles.why_it_suits_brand_and_funnel: It's the CJ-legal enemy line (FUNNEL_PLAN §2). It needs no mechanism and doesn't attack period underwear. The funnel repeats it three times: landing bullet, quiz REACT card, offer table. It names her real workaround (#30), so she recognises herself without being told 'you leak'. Runs on V1 (video) and S1 (the static where this angle's proof is strongest).

angles.name: It's just underwear (plain black briefs, not a kit of liners and spares)
angles.core_message: The just-in-case kit (liners, spare undies, the plan) vs one pair of plain black briefs that look and feel like underwear. Shown side by side, not claimed.
angles.awareness: Problem-aware to solution-aware. Works cold only with the moment and 'pee/leak/sneeze' in the first frame.
angles.proof: The A-vs-B mechanic is Tier A: 21 ads, 5 in a page top-10, but all 5 are old-vs-new (Carol video #1, #2, #4, #5, #10), which we can't run. The runnable 'old solution vs us' version: 7 Tier A ads, best ranks #18 (1920176635259424, 250d), #21 (811197242009709, 230d) and #27 (945622924750214, 169d), 0 in a top-10, all with a diaper foil. The pad-foil version rests on one unranked ad: Everdries 710413878795607 (180d, 'my mom's pads vs what I use', point by point). Live: 'thin' ~270, 'comfortable' ~230, 'invisible' ~110 Everdries videos. On-body silent pull-up: 2028897597834338 (133d, 3 duplicates).
angles.landing_handoff: Bullet 'Feels like underwear. Not a pad, not a diaper.' + subhead 'Black briefs...' (+ carousel slide 3 under leggings, only if it's moved to slide 1 for this traffic; see flags). Then quiz Q7 worries 'feel like a diaper' / 'show under leggings' are answered on the result.
angles.why_it_suits_brand_and_funnel: It answers the two objections that stop her ('feels like a diaper', 'shows under leggings') with visuals, not claims, which is the CJ-safe way. It shares A2's bullet but lands on the other half ('Feels like underwear'). To keep it apart from A2, its A side is her whole workaround kit, not a pad rant. Honest overlap: V1 and V2 both use disposables as the foil, so read them partly as a format test on the same enemy.

angles_rejected.angle: Common, not normal as a LEAD angle (round 1)
angles_rejected.why: Tier B-proven only: Revival 1688978975632845 (139d), MamasandMisses 830409790111485 (163d), Pine Peak 869271709162736 caption (97d), Origin 1311055671051182 (316d, 'Pelvic floor issues don't have to be your new normal'). In the Tier A statics (UltraDries image#1), 'normal' is one line inside a 60+ UTI story. The landing's 'Common? Yes. Normal? No.' has no visible source until the L1 Ridgeview strip is live, and the 1-in-3 stat covers only 6 weeks to 1 year after birth. Used only as an end-card or caption beat once L1 is live. Promote to a lead in round 2.

The live landing never says trampoline, kids, mom or baby outside the fake reviews, which must go. Trampoline comes back only at quiz Q8 of 13, Q13 and the offer page. It's also a repeated-jump moment the wear test hasn't covered. Round 2, after HERO_PASTE_LIST Card 1 ('Ever watched from the side at the trampoline park?...') is live under the hero. Never echo the fake 'trampoline party' review.

angles_rejected.angle: Postpartum identity told to her ('After your baby...', 'Still waiting to bounce back?')
angles_rejected.why: Fails the Meta 'you' rule, and the live hero never says baby or kids (scent break). Upgrade once a /match-p page with Card 1 is live.

angles_rejected.angle: Athlete / CrossFit / runner / gym class (box jumps, double-unders, runs, lifting)
angles_rejected.why: The hero is a laugh line, not training: no gym, class or run language on the landing. The offer FAQ says the product is for 'a few drops to a small splash'. Repeated or heavy leaks raise 'didn't hold' claims under a keep-the-pairs guarantee. Only plain jumping jacks at home (the 'jump' bullet) stay in round 1. Hold the rest for /match-t or /match-run and a wear test that covers them.
No proven 30-45 lead ad, only 4 research rows, no landing line, highest Meta personal-attribute risk. Hold for /match-r.

angles_rejected.angle: Period underwear failed / 'built for pee, not blood' / 'upgrade from period undies'
angles_rejected.why: Banned on CJ (FUNNEL_PLAN §2, Lynmiss only). Our product is a period panty, so 'upgrade' is also an implied superiority claim.

angles_rejected.angle: Pads fail / hold more than pads ('wrong tool for jumping')
angles_rejected.why: An implied comparative efficacy claim with no support. The bank says pads, especially incontinence pads, absorb urine better than period underwear (#22, #23). The CJ enemy line is limited to comfort and waste.
The mechanism block is OFF on CJ, there is no lab data, and nothing on the landing continues it.

angles_rejected.angle: Burned skeptic ('other leak-proof undies failed, ours hold')
angles_rejected.why: Lynmiss only, no mechanism to back it, and the only 'burned' line on the landing is a fake review.
Most-aware, not TOF. There's no price on the landing; price comes after a 13-question quiz. Retargeting only.
Product-aware ('NEW RELEASE' / 'redesigned' posts). 'New' means nothing to a stranger, and we have no old design.

angles_rejected.angle: Skeptic to believer ('looked too thin to work')
angles_rejected.why: Needs real tester or customer voices; we have none yet.
'Eco / sustainable / zero-waste' need substantiation (FTC Green Guides). Only the facts 'wash and wear again' and 'nothing in the trash' are allowed, as a middle beat, never the promise.

angles_rejected.angle: Night-time / heavy leaks / 'stay dry all day'
angles_rejected.why: A light-leak product with unconfirmed back coverage. Quiz Q4 screens heavy leakers out.
Everdries' customer, not ours, and it conflicts with the brand ('not old').
Never-shame rule plus the banned 'discreet' frame. The landing's joke is laughing, not hiding.

video_formats.format: Problem-object open + brand voiceover over b-roll (clean liner in hand, then the briefs on a body)
video_formats.why_this_format: About 8 Tier A voiceover ads open on a pad or diaper (of 137 classified Tier A ads). Two are ranked women's ads: Everdries 1206351388295667 (275d, video#14, 2-6 Meta duplicates, sources disagree; same creative 2156436115112904, 180d) and UltraDries 896552676720439 (193d, video#6, a woman ~40s). Plus the hands-only flat-lay 1730018818434803 (124d). Everdries 1887889898483490 (275d) has the cleanest pad-in-hand hook visual, but it's a founder-story format and unranked. Live: 'pads' on ~190 Everdries videos and ~100/100 Life Beyond Leaks ads. Honest: voiceover has the weakest rank record of the main formats (2 of 29 in a top-10), and the pads angle's top-10 strength sits mostly in statics (hence S1). It works cold because the liner does the hooking and the brand appears late.
video_formats.structure: 40-60s. 0-3s: the moment + the old solution. A clean liner in hand, with one line naming the moment and the leak (brand voice, e.g. 'Keys. Phone. A liner, in case of a sneeze.'). 3-20s: brand VO over liner b-roll, using CJ attributes only: bunches, shifts, feels like a diaper, goes in the trash every day. 20-40s: reveal the plain black brief, hands-only (stretch, fold) and/or on a real woman under leggings, full figure, moving. 40-50s: 'Not a pad, not a diaper. For the sneeze, the laugh and the jump.' 50-55s: '30 nights to see if they hold.' CTA: 'Find my match.'
video_formats.tof_awareness: Problem-aware liner/pad users. Opens on the moment and the object, never on her condition.
video_formats.funnel_handoff: Bullet 'Feels like underwear. Not a pad, not a diaper.' Then quiz Q3 'Pads or liners' gives the REACT card 'Pads bunch and shift the second you move.'
video_formats.production_needs: Props: clean liners and pads (never stained), a handbag, a bathroom trash can, the CJ samples, black leggings. Hands-only talent for the hook. One real woman 30-45 (disclosed) for 10-15s of on-body b-roll, full figure under leggings. Impersonal brand VO (no 'I/we' unless she's a real disclosed tester it's true for). Burned-in captions in brand fonts. The hook can be shot before samples arrive; the payoff can't.
video_formats.compliance_swaps: The only contrast is 'Pads and liners bunch, feel like a diaper, and go in the trash every day.' Never 'wrong tool', 'fails', 'leaks through', 'holds better', 'pads were made for periods' or 'built for pee, not blood'. 'Why are you still...' becomes a third-person or impersonal line, never 'we' from a narrator. No UTI/rash/chemicals/odour, no $ or volume waste figures, no eco words, no '100%' or absorbency, no pour/mug demo. No stained pads, no 🤢. No 'original vs redesigned'. No sale.

static_decision: Two static formats, not three. S1, the plain pad photo with a long brand-voice story caption, is the strongest cold static in the set: 25 Tier A, 13 in a page top-10, and 8 of the pads angle's 15 top-10 slots. It carries A2, where that proof actually sits. S4, the text card, carries A1. Its listicle version is Tier A (Carol image#1, 249d). Its one-line cards are a labelled Tier B-only test (Pine Peak 97d; Origin 312d, but inside a DCO, so the card can't be credited alone). Both formats name the moment before any product, so they need zero brand trust, and both can be made today without samples or talent. S2, the plain on-body photo, was dropped for round 1. With no overlay it reads as a generic underwear ad to a stranger, and all 14 proven versions ran product-aware captions ('redesigned', 'NEW RELEASE'): 6 top-10 slots from only 4 unique photos. Hip and butt crops risk Meta's adult-content rule, and we have no real-woman photo yet (the landing carousel is AI). Plain on-body photos go to retargeting. Six strong statics beat nine with three weak ones.
